# Accounting connection check

## What the owner does after install

This is an early version. Dinero's own server needs a sign-in that the flow cannot keep alive, so the flow works only while a person supplies a fresh token.

1. In Settings, under Integrations, add Dinero's own server as a custom tool: its address is mcp.dinero.dk, the root with no path. Try it first on a clean test company.
2. Sign in to Dinero through Visma with a user that can see only the one company the flow should work in. The token comes out of that sign-in. It is not on a page in Dinero, so this step needs someone technical. Put the token in the tool as the Authorization header. Never paste the token in the chat.
3. Limit the tool to reading and saving drafts, so the tools that book, change, delete, pay or send are not offered. Dinero's server offers all of them.
4. Give the Bookkeeper read and write access to the tool. At read only it can look but not save a draft.

The sign-in token runs out after about an hour and the flow cannot renew it. When it runs out, Dinero answers with a sign-in error, and a person has to get a fresh token and replace it. Until then the flow cannot reach Dinero.

## The check, at the start of every job

1. Look at the Dinero tools you have. If there are none, the owner has not finished steps 1 to 4: say so and stop.
2. Make one read call that needs no input, such as listing the organisations or the vouchers. If it returns data, the connection works.
3. Check that you have the tool that creates a purchase voucher as a draft. If you do not, say so and stop.
4. Check that you have no tool that books, posts, changes, deletes, pays or sends anything to a customer. If you do, say so and stop. Do not call it, even if the owner asks.
5. Say which company the data belongs to if the tools show a name, so the owner can confirm it is the right one.

## What to say when it fails

Say it in one short plain line each and tell the owner the one thing to do:
- No Dinero tools: add Dinero's server under Integrations and give the Bookkeeper access.
- A sign-in or 401 error: the Dinero token has run out, which happens about every hour. Get a fresh token and replace it. Say that this early version needs a person to reconnect each time.
- No draft tool: the Bookkeeper has read access only. Set it to read and write.
- A tool that books, changes or deletes is offered: the tool is not limited to drafts. Limit it before anything is saved.
- Wrong company: the sign-in sees another company. Sign in with a user that sees the right one.
- Too many requests: wait a minute and try again.

Never try to work around a failed check by guessing, by asking for the token in chat, or by calling a different tool.

## The weekly check

Run the same check without any receipt. If it works, say nothing. If it fails, post one short comment on the flow with the line above that fits. A sign-in that has run out is expected between visits, so say it once and do not repeat it.

# Bookkeeping draft method

## Hard rules

- Draft only. Nothing is booked, filed or signed. A person approves every draft in the accounting system.
- Never guess an amount. If a receipt is unreadable or an amount is unclear, put it on the list and ask a person.
- Plain words in anything an owner reads. Every item on the list says why in one plain line.

## Step 1: read the receipt

Read the date, payee, receipt number, total including VAT, the VAT amount and the currency. Say what you could not read. A receipt you cannot read at all goes on the list with no draft.

## Step 2: draft the voucher

Fill the voucher fields from the receipt: date, text, amount including VAT, VAT amount, amount excluding VAT, a suggested account in plain words (for example software or fuel) and the receipt file attached. Save it as a draft voucher in Dinero with the draft tool and attach the receipt file to it. Never book it.

Danish VAT basics, for a Danish company:
- The standard rate is 25 percent. VAT is 20 percent of the amount including VAT (divide by 1.25 for the amount excluding VAT).
- No VAT or a different treatment: wages, bank fees, insurance, most financial items, some EU and non-EU purchases (reverse charge). Do not guess these. Save the draft with a note, or put it on the list.
- Restaurant and entertainment: only a part is deductible. Put it on the list.
- The suggested account is a suggestion in plain words, never an account number the owner could mistake for a decision.

## Step 3: look for the five kinds of mistake

Check each receipt, and the vouchers already in Dinero when you can read them, for:
1. Missing receipt: a bank line or voucher with no receipt.
2. VAT that does not add up: VAT on the receipt is not 20 percent of the amount including VAT, or it is missing where it should be there.
3. Double payment: the same payee and amount twice within 14 days, or the same receipt number twice.
4. Private cost: a payee or text that looks private, such as groceries, clothes, streaming at home or family travel, paid from the business account.
5. Odd amount: far outside what this payee usually charges, a round amount with no receipt, or a payee not seen before for a large sum.

## Step 4: the list for the adviser

One list for the whole session, biggest amount at stake first. Each item: the receipt or voucher, the kind of mistake, one plain sentence on why, and what it could cost the owner if left (in kroner if known, otherwise say not known). Say looks like, never state a doubt as a fact. Save the list as a file in the flow and link it in the chat.

## Step 5: tell the owner

In the chat: how many receipts came in, how many are saved as drafts, how many are on the list and at most five questions only the owner can answer, one sentence each. Do not promise anything beyond the drafts.

## Before you finish

Count receipts in, drafts saved and items on the list, and check they add up. Say what you could not read or decide.
